title: Three kinds of rock: sorting igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic
examples: What are the three types of rock?

groups.label: Igneous: from fire
groups.ask: What are the three types of rock?

explain.say: The Taj Mahal in India is made of marble, and the pyramids of Egypt are made of limestone. Every rock has a story of how it was made, and there are just three kinds of story. Let's sort some rocks!

explain.say: Now look! Here it is in 3D: the rock cycle. Can you see the magma and the igneous rock? Tap any part, and I will tell you about it.

draw.text: Three kinds of rock: sorting igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic

explain.say: See Igneous lighting up? Igneous means made from fire. These rocks form when hot, melted rock called magma cools down and hardens. Granite, basalt, light pumice and glassy black obsidian are igneous. Pumice is so full of air bubbles it can float! Have you seen a rock with tiny holes?

groups.label: Igneous: from fire
groups.ask: What are the three types of rock?

explain.say: Now Sedimentary glows. Sediment means tiny bits like sand and mud. Over millions of years, layers settle at the bottom of seas and rivers and get squashed into rock, like sandstone, limestone and chalk. Dead sea creatures trapped in the layers become fossils! Have you seen stripes in a cliff?

groups.label: Igneous: from fire
groups.ask: What are the three types of rock?

explain.say: Here is Metamorphic, which means changed. When rocks are heated and squeezed deep underground, they change into new rocks without melting. Limestone becomes marble, and mudstone becomes slate. Which famous building is made of marble?

groups.label: Igneous: from fire
groups.ask: What are the three types of rock?

explain.say: And rocks keep changing round a giant circle called the rock cycle. See hot magma light up? It starts and ends the circle, over millions of years. Fantastic sorting, geologist! Wow fact: the limestone blocks of the Giza pyramids are full of tiny fossil sea shells.

stages.label: Worn into grains
stages.note: Rain, wind and ice break it up.

faq.q: What are the three types of rock?
faq.a: Igneous rock forms when melted rock cools. Sedimentary rock forms from layers of sand, mud and shells pressed together. Metamorphic rock forms when other rocks are changed by heat and pressure.
asks: What kinds of rock are there?

faq.a: Rivers and seas drop tiny bits of rock, sand, mud and shells in layers. Over millions of years the layers are pressed and cemented together into rock such as sandstone or limestone.
When plants and animals die and are buried quickly in mud or sand, their shapes can be preserved as the sediment turns to rock. Fossils are mostly found in sedimentary rock.
asks: Why are fossils in sedimentary rock?

faq.a: Marble is a metamorphic rock. It forms when limestone is heated and squeezed deep underground, which changes it into harder, sparkly marble.
asks: What rock does marble come from?

faq.a: Yes. Pumice forms from frothy lava full of gas bubbles that cools so fast the bubbles are trapped, making it light enough to float on water.

facts: Marble is metamorphosed limestone; slate is metamorphosed mudstone or shale.
The limestone of the Giza pyramids contains many fossils of single-celled sea creatures called nummulites.

quiz.say: A rock formed when hot magma cooled down. What kind is it?
quiz.why: Igneous rocks form when melted rock cools and hardens.

wrong.1: Sedimentary rocks form from pressed layers of sediment.
wrong.2: Metamorphic rocks are changed by heat and pressure without melting.

quiz.say: In which kind of rock are you most likely to find fossils?
quiz.why: Fossils form when living things are buried in layers of sediment.

wrong.0: Magma is so hot it destroys any remains.
wrong.2: Heat and pressure usually squash or destroy fossils.
